newsitem.title: USA: Weld calls for fair hearing on Mexico envoy post.
newsitem.headline: Weld calls for fair hearing on Mexico envoy post.

text.p: Former Massachusetts governor William Weld began briefings on Thursday on his bid to become the next U.S. ambassador to Mexico, saying he wanted a "fair hearing" in the Senate on his nomination.

"A fair hearing is all I'm looking for," he told reporters as he called at the State Department to meet senior officials. "I call on Senator (Jesse) Helms to explain why there shouldn't be a fair hearing."

Helms, a North Carolina Republican who is chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has vowed to prevent Weld's nomination by President Bill Clinton from reaching the floor of the full Senate for a vote.

Though Weld is also a Republican, Helms charges that he is "soft" on drugs, and hence inappropriate for the post in Mexico, a major transit route for narcotics reaching the United States. Weld denies the charge.
Weld, who resigned the Massachusetts governorship on Tuesday to fight for his nomination, was meeting at the State Department with Mexico desk officer John Leonard.
He was later to call on senators on Capitol Hill before returning to the State Department to see Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott and Under Secretary of State Thomas Pickering.

Despite predictions that his nomination is doomed, Weld said: "I don't really have a sense one way or the other. I'm just looking forward to meeting with the State Department folks today and the senators."

Weld, a Spanish-speaker, said his aim was to learn "a little bit more about Mexico than even I've picked up in the last few weeks and talk to some senators, drop a penny in the well, listen for the echo."
